messages:
marta: quick one — we're hashing out precheck behavior for per-key bursts. today precheck returns 429 when the queue is 'full'. infra suggests returning 503 if the runtime is saturated to avoid dangling leases. which is less surprising for clients and better for retries?

sam: +1 on clarifying semantics. 429 implies client should slow down, 503 implies server overload. for burst credits i think we want a hybrid: short token lease (soft-queue) that promises a slot, then bounce with 503 if runtime can't materialize it within lease window.

yara: i like hybrid. concrete: grant a lease for N ms and a max lease count per key. if runtime accepts before lease expiry, proceed; else release and return 503. clients can opt into longer wait via Retry-After.

kev: operationally we need metrics for this: lease_granted, lease_expired, lease_revoked, queue_accept_rate, precheck_503_rate, precheck_429_rate. those need to be surfaced in console as per-key and per-org heatmaps.

archibald: corner case — what about per-key fairness? big keys can hog leases if they keep getting recycled. add decay window for lease credits (sliding token bucket with two windows: burst and sustained).

marta: agreed. rough config sketch:
```
precheck:
  lease_ms: 2500  # how long a promise holds
  lease_tokens_per_key: 3
  burst_window_ms: 60000
  sustained_window_ms: 600000
  fallback_on_expiry: 503|queued  # policy toggle
```

sam: +1. also add a "prefer_queue_if_latency_ok" toggle so certain keys (internal partners) can opt-in to longer soft-queueing vs immediate fail.

kev: about 429 vs 503: 429 should be used when client exceeded configured quota (rate-limited by policy). 503 should be used when runtime capacity is the limiting factor (operator-level overload). mixing them blurs signal for clients and for consumers of our telemetry.

yara: yes. we should emit a shed_reason tag: quota_exhausted, runtime_saturated, policy_override. makes downstream analytics easier and drives automatic fallbacks.

archibald: UX ask — in console rollout page show: per-key burst credits (current / max), recent lease expiries, and example timelines for requests that were leased then failed. make it a flag on rollout controls so PMs can choose safe defaults.

marta: ops question — do we keep a short global grace credit for new keys so onboarding demos don't immediately 429? maybe 1 sample/day for 24h. thoughts?

sam: we do something similar today for trial keys. make it explicit and measurable; call it onboarding_allowance. show it in billing/usage so we don't surprise customers.

kev: telemetry names again: precheck_lease_granted{key,org}, precheck_lease_released{reason}, precheck_reject_{429,503}, queue_latency_ms_p50/95/99. wire these into alerting (spike in lease_expired -> server-side pressure).

marta: sounds good — i'll draft a short RFC with config defaults and the console mockups. leaving rollout flag off by default. thanks all :thumbsup:

ratebot: auto-note: rolled deploys flagged: precheck-service v3.7 will include lease APIs. deploy ETA 2w unless RFC changes.

marta: filing RFC: https://go/redwood/rfc/precheck-lease (draft) — comments welcome :eyes:
